mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 110 2.2 TDCi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt Land Rover Defender 110 2.2 TDCi engine typically costs between £3,000 and £5,000 for supply only. Reconditioned units start around £2,000, while used engines can be found from £800. Prices vary based on whether you choose supply-only or a full supply and fit service.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of turbo or EGR failure in a Land Rover Defender 110 2.2 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early warning signs include a loss of power (limp mode), excessive black smoke from the exhaust, and unusual whining noises from the turbocharger. Coolant loss without visible external leaks can also indicate a failing EGR cooler.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Land Rover Defender 110 2.2 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, given the current classic vehicle market. A well-maintained Land Rover Defender 110 2.2 TDCi holds a value of £12,000 to £25,000+. Investing £3,000-£5,000 in a rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty is financially viable and protects the appreciating asset value of the vehicle.

mainEntity.name: What is the DT224 engine code in the Land Rover Defender 110 2.2 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The DT224 is the specific Ford-sourced Duratorq 2.2-litre diesel engine code fitted to the final generation of classic Defenders (2012-2016). It was introduced to meet Euro 5 emissions standards, replacing the earlier 2.4 TDCi, and features a revised turbocharger and DPF system.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 110 2.2 TDCi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Land Rover Defender 110 2.2 TDCi typically takes 2 to 3 working days. This includes the removal of the old unit, thorough cleaning of the engine bay, installation of the replacement engine, and comprehensive testing.

commonProblems.h3: The Land Rover Defender 110 2.2 TDCi is a robust workhorse, but its Ford-sourced Duratorq engine has well-documented vulnerabilities, particularly with the EGR system and turbo actuators. Rebuilt engines sourced through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: EGR Cooler & Turbo Actuator Failure - Why the Land Rover Defender 110 2.2 TDCi DT224 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Carbon buildup and thermal stress cause the EGR cooler to leak coolant into the intake, while the turbo wastegate actuator linkage wears, leading to boost loss and limp mode.
